# package iso

```go
import "github.com/otfabric/go-mms/transport/iso"
```

Package iso provides TCP+TP0 transport integration for go-mms.

This package bridges the gap between raw TCP connections and the mms.Transport interface used by the MMS client and server. It handles:

  - TCP connection establishment and acceptance
  - Optional TLS wrapping
  - COTP class 0 (TP0) via otfabric/go-cotp (Connect/Accept, TSDU I/O)
  - TSAP selector configuration

TPKT framing and the COTP handshake are owned by go-cotp; this package maps [mms.Transport](https://pkg.go.dev/github.com/otfabric/go-mms#Transport) Send/Receive onto WriteTSDU/ReadTSDU.

#### Client usage {#hdr-Client_usage}

	conn, err := iso.DialTCP(ctx, "10.0.0.1:102",
	    iso.WithCalledTSelector([]byte{0x00, 0x01}),
	)
	if err != nil { ... }
	client, err := mms.NewClient(ctx, conn, mms.DialOptions{...})

Or use the convenience function:

	client, err := iso.Dial(ctx, "10.0.0.1:102",
	    iso.WithCalledTSelector([]byte{0x00, 0x01}),
	    iso.WithClientDialOptions(mms.DialOptions{...}),
	)

#### Server usage {#hdr-Server_usage}

	ln, err := iso.Listen(":102")
	if err != nil { ... }
	err = server.ListenAndServe(ctx, ln) // owns ln; closes it on return

#### TLS {#hdr-TLS}

Use [WithTLSConfig](#func-withtlsconfig) to enable TLS transport security. When TLS is configured, the connection layering becomes:

	TCP → TLS → TPKT → COTP → Session → Presentation → ACSE → MMS

The standard port for MMS over TLS is 3782 (vs 102 for plaintext). Plaintext and TLS listeners can coexist on the same server.

Peer certificates from TLS connections are accessible via the [mms.TLSTransport](https://pkg.go.dev/github.com/otfabric/go-mms#TLSTransport) interface for server-side authentication policy.

#### Security note on ACSE password authentication {#hdr-Security_note_on_ACSE_password_authentication}

ACSE password authentication ([mms.ISOOptions](https://pkg.go.dev/github.com/otfabric/go-mms#ISOOptions).Password) embeds credentials inside the association request PDU. Without TLS, the password travels in the clear as part of the TPKT/COTP payload — this is plaintext-equivalent on port 102. ACSE password authentication should be combined with TLS transport to provide confidentiality. The library does not enforce this combination.

#### Addressing {#hdr-Addressing}

A client sends a calling and called T-selector of 00 01 and proposes a 1024-octet TPDU, and go-mms adds S-selector 00 01, P-selector 00 00 00 01 and AP-titles 1.1.1.999 / 1.1.1.999.1 with AE-qualifier 12 (see [mms.ISOOptions](https://pkg.go.dev/github.com/otfabric/go-mms#ISOOptions)): the addressing libiec61850 uses and IEDs expect. Use [WithCallingTSelector](#func-withcallingtselector), [WithCalledTSelector](#func-withcalledtselector) and [WithMaxTPDULength](#func-withmaxtpdulength) for an IED configured otherwise (the OSI-TSEL of its SCL ConnectedAP):

	conn, err := iso.Dial(ctx, "10.0.0.1:102",
	    iso.WithCallingTSelector([]byte{0x00, 0x01}),
	    iso.WithCalledTSelector([]byte{0x00, 0x00, 0x00, 0x01}),
	)

A [Listener](#type-listener) accepts any called selector and returns the CR's selectors in the CC. [WithCalledTSelector](#func-withcalledtselector) makes it strict: a CR whose called selector is absent or different is refused with a Disconnect Request (reason 3, address unknown).

#### Architecture {#hdr-Architecture}

The layering is: TCP → \[TLS] → TPKT → COTP → Session → Presentation → ACSE → MMS. This package owns TCP (+ optional TLS) and adapts go-cotp's TP0 Conn to [mms.Transport](https://pkg.go.dev/github.com/otfabric/go-mms#Transport). go-mms core owns the upper four layers.

## Constants

```go
const (
	// DefaultMaxTPDULength is the TPDU size a client proposes in the CR
	// (parameter 0xC0 = 0x0A, 1024 octets).
	DefaultMaxTPDULength = 1024
	// MaxTSelectorLength is the longest T-selector a client sends
	// (IEC 61850-8-1 §6.2.3.2.2).
	MaxTSelectorLength = 4
)
```

Default client transport parameters, the values libiec61850 and most IEC 61850 clients send and IEDs expect (IEC 61850-8-1 mandates none; it limits a T-selector to 4 octets, §6.2.3.2.2).

## Functions

### func Dial

```go
func Dial(ctx context.Context, addr string, opts ...Option) (*mms.Client, error)
```

Dial is a convenience function that establishes a TCP+TP0 connection and creates an MMS client in one call.

It combines [DialTCP](#func-dialtcp) with [mms.NewClient](https://pkg.go.dev/github.com/otfabric/go-mms#NewClient). Use [WithClientDialOptions](#func-withclientdialoptions) to pass MMS-level configuration; T-selectors from [mms.DialOptions](https://pkg.go.dev/github.com/otfabric/go-mms#DialOptions).Transport are used when [WithCallingTSelector](#func-withcallingtselector) or [WithCalledTSelector](#func-withcalledtselector) are not set, and the defaults when neither is. With [WithRetry](#func-withretry), failed attempts (connect, handshakes and association) are retried with backoff.

### func DialTCP

```go
func DialTCP(ctx context.Context, addr string, opts ...Option) (mms.Transport, error)
```

DialTCP establishes a TCP connection to addr, performs the TP0 handshake via go-cotp, and returns a [mms.Transport](https://pkg.go.dev/github.com/otfabric/go-mms#Transport) ready for MMS communication.

addr is a host:port string (e.g. "10.0.0.1:102"). The standard MMS port is 102 for plaintext.

The COTP CR carries a calling and a called T-selector (default 00 01 each, see [WithCallingTSelector](#func-withcallingtselector) and [WithCalledTSelector](#func-withcalledtselector)) and a TPDU size (default DefaultMaxTPDULength, see [WithMaxTPDULength](#func-withmaxtpdulength)), as IEC 61850 IEDs expect: some refuse a CR without them with a Disconnect Request, reason 3 (address unknown).

With [WithRetry](#func-withretry), failed attempts are retried with backoff.

## Types

### type Listener

```go
type Listener struct {

	// handshaken transports, handed to Accept
	// semaphore of in-flight handshakes
	// closed when the accept loop stops
	// why the accept loop stopped; set before done is closed

}
```

Listener accepts TCP connections, performs the TP0 handshake for each, and returns [mms.Transport](https://pkg.go.dev/github.com/otfabric/go-mms#Transport) instances ready for MMS server use.

Handshakes run concurrently in the background, bounded by [WithHandshakeTimeout](#func-withhandshaketimeout), so a peer that connects and stays silent never blocks other connections.

Listener implements [mms.TransportListener](https://pkg.go.dev/github.com/otfabric/go-mms#TransportListener).

#### func Listen

```go
func Listen(addr string, opts ...Option) (*Listener, error)
```

Listen creates a new [Listener](#type-listener) bound to the given TCP address. addr follows [net.Listen](https://pkg.go.dev/net#Listen) conventions (e.g. ":102", "0.0.0.0:102").

#### func NewListener

```go
func NewListener(ln net.Listener, opts ...Option) *Listener
```

NewListener wraps an existing [net.Listener](https://pkg.go.dev/net#Listener) with COTP handshake support. This is useful when the caller manages the TCP listener directly (e.g. for testing, custom bind logic, or fault injection).

#### func (Listener) Accept

```go
func (l *Listener) Accept(ctx context.Context) (mms.Transport, error)
```

Accept returns the next connection that completed the TCP, optional TLS, and TP0 handshakes.

Accept blocks until a connection is available, the listener is closed, or the context is cancelled. Context cancellation does NOT close the listener — the caller may retry Accept with a new context.

Connections whose handshake fails or times out are closed and logged (see [WithLogger](#func-withlogger)); they never cause Accept to return. Only listener-level or context-level errors do.

#### func (Listener) Addr

```go
func (l *Listener) Addr() net.Addr
```

Addr returns the listener's network address.

#### func (Listener) Close

```go
func (l *Listener) Close() error
```

Close closes the underlying TCP listener and any connection still handshaking or waiting for Accept. A blocked [Listener.Accept](#func-listener-accept) returns an error. Close is idempotent.

### type Option

```go
type Option func(*Options)
```

Option configures an ISO transport connection.

#### func WithCalledTSelector

```go
func WithCalledTSelector(sel []byte) Option
```

WithCalledTSelector sets the called TSAP selector (COTP CR parameter 0xC2), at most MaxTSelectorLength octets for a client.

A client sends 00 01 when no called selector is configured (here or in [mms.TransportOptions](https://pkg.go.dev/github.com/otfabric/go-mms#TransportOptions)); a non-nil empty sel omits the parameter.

On a [Listener](#type-listener) it makes the selector strict: a CR whose called selector is absent or differs byte for byte is refused with a Disconnect Request (reason 3, address unknown). Without it a Listener accepts any called selector, as other IEC 61850 servers do.

#### func WithCallingTSelector

```go
func WithCallingTSelector(sel []byte) Option
```

WithCallingTSelector sets the calling TSAP selector (COTP CR parameter 0xC1), at most MaxTSelectorLength octets.

A client sends 00 01 when no calling selector is configured (here or in [mms.TransportOptions](https://pkg.go.dev/github.com/otfabric/go-mms#TransportOptions)); a non-nil empty sel omits the parameter.

#### func WithClientDialOptions

```go
func WithClientDialOptions(opts mms.DialOptions) Option
```

WithClientDialOptions sets the MMS dial options used by the convenience [Dial](#func-dial) function. These options are passed to [mms.NewClient](https://pkg.go.dev/github.com/otfabric/go-mms#NewClient) after the transport is established. Ignored by [DialTCP](#func-dialtcp) and [Listen](#func-listen).

#### func WithDialer

```go
func WithDialer(dial func(ctx context.Context, network, addr string) (net.Conn, error)) Option
```

WithDialer replaces the function [DialTCP](#func-dialtcp) and [Dial](#func-dial) use to open the TCP connection (by default a zero [net.Dialer](https://pkg.go.dev/net#Dialer)'s DialContext). Use it for a destination allowlist checked against the resolved IP (for example a [net.Dialer](https://pkg.go.dev/net#Dialer) with a Control hook), a SOCKS or HTTP proxy, a jump host, a source address, custom socket options, or an in-memory connection and fault injection in tests. A [\*net.Dialer](https://pkg.go.dev/net#Dialer)'s or a proxy's DialContext fits as a method value. With \[WithTLS], the TLS handshake runs over the connection it returns.

It is called once per attempt (see [WithRetry](#func-withretry)) with network "tcp" and the address given to [DialTCP](#func-dialtcp) or [Dial](#func-dial). The context carries the caller's deadline and cancellation; a custom dialer must honour it. Like [net.Dialer](https://pkg.go.dev/net#Dialer), it returns a non-nil connection exactly when the error is nil: a connection returned together with an error is closed, and a nil connection with a nil error fails the dial. Its error is wrapped, so [errors.Is](https://pkg.go.dev/errors#Is) reaches it, for example an allowlist's refusal. The returned connection is owned and closed by the transport. Nil keeps the default. Ignored by [Listen](#func-listen).

#### func WithHandshakeTimeout

```go
func WithHandshakeTimeout(d time.Duration) Option
```

WithHandshakeTimeout bounds the TLS and COTP handshakes of each connection accepted by a [Listener](#type-listener); a peer that does not complete them in time is disconnected. Zero means 10s; a negative value disables the limit. Handshakes run concurrently, so a slow peer never delays other connections. For clients, bound the handshake with the context passed to [DialTCP](#func-dialtcp) or [Dial](#func-dial).

#### func WithLogger

```go
func WithLogger(l *slog.Logger) Option
```

WithLogger sets a structured logger for the ISO transport layer. Used by [Listener](#type-listener) to log per-connection handshake failures and by [DialTCP](#func-dialtcp) and [Dial](#func-dial) to log failed attempts retried under [WithRetry](#func-withretry).

#### func WithMaxTPDULength

```go
func WithMaxTPDULength(n int) Option
```

WithMaxTPDULength sets the maximum TPDU size in octets. A client proposes it in the CR (default DefaultMaxTPDULength); 65531 omits the 0xC0 parameter, the RFC 1006 default that earlier go-mms versions sent. On a [Listener](#type-listener) it caps the size accepted from a CR (default: whatever the peer proposes, up to 65531). Valid values are 128..65531.

#### func WithRetry

```go
func WithRetry(p mms.RetryPolicy) Option
```

WithRetry makes [DialTCP](#func-dialtcp) and [Dial](#func-dial) retry failed attempts according to p (exponential backoff with jitter, honouring the context). For [Dial](#func-dial) one attempt covers TCP connect, TLS and COTP handshakes and the MMS association; errors that cannot succeed on retry, such as a rejected association, are returned at once (see [mms.IsRetryable](https://pkg.go.dev/github.com/otfabric/go-mms#IsRetryable)). The default is a single attempt. Ignored by [Listen](#func-listen).

#### func WithTLSConfig

```go
func WithTLSConfig(cfg *tls.Config) Option
```

WithTLSConfig enables TLS on the transport connection.

For clients ([DialTCP](#func-dialtcp), [Dial](#func-dial)): the config is used to perform a TLS handshake after the TCP connection is established, before the COTP handshake. Set ServerName to the expected server hostname for certificate verification.

For servers ([Listen](#func-listen), [NewListener](#func-newlistener)): the config is used to accept TLS connections. Include server certificates and optionally set ClientAuth to request client certificates.

The standard port for MMS over TLS is 3782 (vs 102 for plaintext).
